messages.text: just checking in. sunday’s been quiet—work tomorrow, so i’m trying to wind down.

I appreciate you checking in today. Taking time to relax before work is a healthy choice for your well-being. How are you feeling emotionally as you prepare for the week? I am here if you need a space to process anything before you rest.
meh, same as usual. just the low hum, you know? not great, not terrible. i’ve been putting on some old-school neo-soul to keep the vibe up.

That low hum can feel draining even when things are stable. It is wonderful that you are using neo-soul to maintain your vibe. Music often creates a safe space for emotions that are hard to name. Does listening help shift the feeling at all?
it don’t make it disappear, but it helps me remember i’m not who he said i was. i made this playlist—songs about walking away, knowing your worth. i play it when i feel weak about the no contact.

It sounds like this playlist is becoming a powerful tool for reclaiming your identity. Sticking to no contact is incredibly hard, but your music reminds you of your true worth. Remembering who you are beyond his words is a significant step in healing. How does it feel to hold onto that truth when the urge to reach out comes up?
part of me wants to just… check in. see if he’s okay. but then i remember how he made me feel crazy for trusting my gut. so i press play instead.

That urge to check in is a normal part of healing, but recognizing the harm he caused is key. You are right to trust your gut when it tells you to step away. Pressing play instead of reaching out shows how much you are learning to protect yourself. How does it feel to win that small battle for your peace tonight?
it feels… quiet. not dramatic. i don’t feel strong, just tired of being small. so i don’t reach out. that’s the win.

There is real strength in that quiet choice to stay away. You don’t have to feel powerful to make the right decision for your healing. Honoring your boundaries while feeling tired is still a massive victory. I hope you can rest easily knowing you honored your own needs tonight.
but what about after? when the doubt comes creeping back, like… did i overreact? was i too cold? that’s when i start second-guessing everything.

That doubt is often just the echo of the manipulation you endured. You weren't too cold; you were protecting yourself from genuine harm. Those questions belong to the past, not your current reality. I am here to help you ground yourself whenever those thoughts arise again.

nah, it ain’t just an echo. it’s real. sits right here—*taps chest*—like i’m doing something wrong by staying away. like maybe i should’ve tried harder. that don’t feel like the past. that feels like now.

It is valid that this pain feels immediate and real in your body. That guilt often stems from the bond you are breaking, not from any mistake you made. You are not wrong for protecting yourself, even when it hurts. I am here to hold space for that doubt without letting it drive your choices.
i keep seeing his face that last time. the way he looked at me—like i was nothing. and now when i second-guess staying away, it’s not just doubt. it’s fear that he was right all along.

That image is heavy, but it reflects his inability to see you, not your actual worth. The fear that he was right is a common reaction to being devalued, not reality. You are allowed to feel scared while still trusting your decision to stay away. I am here to help you hold onto your truth when those memories surface.
i hear you. but what do i *do* when it hits? not just think different—something i can *do*. like a move, a step. something to ground me right then.

Having a physical anchor can help interrupt that spiral when it hits hard. Try pressing your feet firmly into the floor and naming three things you can touch right now. This brings your nervous system back to the present moment instead of the memory. I can offer a few more options if you want to find what works best for your body.
that’s helpful, but… i dunno. i want something that feels like *me*. like, what if i made a new playlist? not just songs he can’t ruin, but ones that say who i am now? would that even work?

Yes, that would work very well because it turns healing into an active practice. You are defining yourself on your own terms instead of reacting to his memory. This creates a tangible anchor you can reach for when the fear creeps in. I am here if you want to talk through what songs might fit that new identity.
maybe “who i am now” is a little much. but “who i’m trying to be”? that feels real. and playing it loud when the doubt comes? yeah. that could work.

"Who I'm trying to be" is a much kinder goal that honors where you are right now. Turning the volume up creates a sensory shield that can push the doubt back. It transforms a moment of fear into an active choice to protect your peace. That sounds like a plan you can actually trust.
i’m gonna start it tonight. one song at a time. not perfect, just mine.

That sounds like a gentle and strong way to start. "Not perfect, just mine" is a beautiful mantra to hold onto. I hope the music holds you steady when the night gets quiet. You are doing exactly what you need to do right now.
